beats.subline: Friday, November 13, 2026 close — AI stocks extended their slide as Nvidia fell further following Jensen Huang's ouster, while hot wholesale inflation data added pressure.
beats.body: Nvidia dropped another 2% to a fresh 52-week low, AMD tumbled 8.8% and Broadcom fell nearly 5% as the AI-stock selloff triggered by Huang's abrupt departure stretched into a second week; the dollar firmed after October wholesale inflation came in hotter than expected, with traders now watching Nvidia's upcoming earnings and Anthropic's IPO roadshow.

beats.headline: Iran's Assembly of Experts urges weighing NPT exit as Tehran reveals US outreach through Putin
beats.body: Iran's Assembly of Experts urged the country's leadership to consider withdrawing from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, and Tehran's chief negotiator said US officials had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to persuade Iran to open direct talks with Washington, a request the White House did not acknowledge; separately, the UN Security Council unanimously condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

beats.body: No PLA activity or Taiwan Strait development within the 72-hour window could be confirmed from a dated source; Taiwan's reported 'area denial' drills involving China's Liaoning carrier group trace back to November 10-11 and fall outside the window.

beats.headline: Iran claims two more tankers hit mines in Hormuz as US Navy keeps clearing shipping lanes
beats.body: Iran's army said two more tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and a UK maritime security firm confirmed a separate commercial vessel was hit near the UAE, causing an engine-room fire; the US Navy says it continues clearing mines from the strait's shipping routes as its blockade of Iranian ports continues.

beats.headline: Anthropic eyes Nov. 18 IPO pricing as Claude Meetings beta rolls out
beats.body: Anthropic's roadshow for its Nasdaq listing under ticker ANT points toward pricing on November 18 and trading starting November 19 at a valuation near $1.2 trillion, with Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and other chipmakers already committing $26 billion to a related private placement; the company also began rolling out a Claude Meetings beta letting Claude join Google Meet calls as a visible participant to take notes and build documents live.
